<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917894_theRebbe_634" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917894_theRebbe_634__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Opening heading for the maamar for Acharon Shel Pesach 5712.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B"S"D.</t>
    <t s="1">Acharon Shel Pesach 5712*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The verse "As in the days of your exodus from Egypt, I will show him wonders" is puzzling, since the future redemption is far greater, and the wording shifts from "you" to "him."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders"1,</t>
    <t s="1">and it needs to be understood:</t>
    <t s="2">Behold, the future redemption will be much loftier than the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt</t>
    <t s="3">[therefore,</t>
    <t s="4">according to the opinion of Ben Zoma2,</t>
    <t s="5">we do not mention the Exodus from Egypt in the days of Moshiach.</t>
    <t s="6">And also according to the opinion of the Sages2</t>
    <t s="7">who do mention the Exodus from Egypt in the days of Moshiach,</t>
    <t s="8">because there is an advantage in the Exodus from Egypt even relative to the future redemption,</t>
    <t s="9">[nevertheless] the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt will be secondary to the future redemption2],</t>
    <t s="10">and what is the meaning of its saying "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="11">[implying] that the superiority of the future redemption is that even then there will be "I will show him wonders" as it was in the Exodus from Egypt.</t>
    <t s="12">Also, it needs to be understood that it specifies "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="13">[meaning] that the main advantage of the future redemption is not in the wonders themselves that will be then, but in that the Holy One, blessed be He, will show the wonders.</t>
    <t s="14">Also, it needs to be understood its saying "I will show him" in the third person,</t>
    <t s="15">behold, at the beginning it says</t>
    <t s="16">("As in the days of")</t>
    <t s="17">"your exodus" in the second person,</t>
    <t s="18">and it should have said "I will show you."</t>
    <t s="19">And what is said in the Zohar3,</t>
    <t s="20">that what is said "I will show him" in the third person is because "I will show him" refers to Moshe,</t>
    <t s="21">requires explanation of the connection of this interpretation with the simple interpretation that "I will show him" refers to Israel.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>There are two types of miracles—those above nature and those clothed in nature—and the future redemption's wonders will be drawn from Him alone, yet revealed.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the point of the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="1">that in miracles there are</t>
    <t s="2">(generally)</t>
    <t s="3">two types.</t>
    <t s="4">Miracles that are above nature</t>
    <t s="5">[like the miracles that were in the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="6">the turning of water to blood etc., and up to the miracle of the Splitting of the Sea, when the sea was turned into dry land],</t>
    <t s="7">and miracles that are clothed in the ways of nature.</t>
    <t s="8">And within them themselves there are two manners.</t>
    <t s="9">[There are those where] the garments of nature are in a manner that it is recognizable that they are only a garment for the miracle that is clothed within them.</t>
    <t s="10">Like the miracles of Chanukah and Purim,</t>
    <t s="11">that despite their being clothed in the ways of nature,</t>
    <t s="12">nevertheless the miracle within them was recognizably revealed</t>
    <t s="13">(and even "all the ends of the earth saw"4)</t>
    <t s="14">[the miracle within them].</t>
    <t s="15">And [there are those where] the garments of nature conceal the miracle that is clothed within them5.</t>
    <t s="16">And it is known6</t>
    <t s="17">that the source of miracles clothed in nature is from a place loftier than the source of miracles that are above nature.</t>
    <t s="18">And the source of miracles that are clothed in nature in a manner that it is not even recognizable that the garments of nature are only a garment is from a place even loftier7.</t>
    <t s="19">As it is written8</t>
    <t s="20">"To Him Who alone does great wonders," and our Sages, of blessed memory, said9</t>
    <t s="21">"Even the beneficiary of the miracle does not recognize his miracle,"</t>
    <t s="22">[meaning] that the source of these wonders</t>
    <t s="23">(where the beneficiary of the miracle does not recognize his miracle)</t>
    <t s="24">is from the aspect of "alone"10.</t>
    <t s="25">And this is the novel point in this, that in the future redemption there will be "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="26">for the wonders of the future redemption will be drawn from Him, blessed be He, alone,</t>
    <t s="27">as our Sages, of blessed memory, said11</t>
    <t s="28">"In the past</t>
    <t s="29">(in the Exodus from Egypt)</t>
    <t s="30">I and My court were going before them, but in the future to come, I alone [will go]."</t>
    <t s="31">For the miracles that were in the Exodus from Egypt were drawn from Him, blessed be He, through His court, and the miracles of the future redemption will be from Him alone</t>
    <t s="32">(not through His court)12.</t>
    <t s="33">And this is the novel point of "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="34">that although the wonders that are drawn from Him, blessed be He, alone are</t>
    <t s="35">(generally)</t>
    <t s="36">in a manner that He alone knows that this is a miracle,</t>
    <t s="37">nevertheless, there will be "I will show him wonders,"</t>
    <t s="38">[meaning] that the miracle within them will be seen in revelation.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
